definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (4.26 and 4.29) define a character as a code value of a coded character set; 4.27 (screen item) and 4.28 (COBOL character repertoire) do not apply to a literal's content. GR7 compares 'each character's encoding', the coded-character-set sense, which 2023 uses undefined with the same meaning; the literals and comparisons the rule governs are unchanged.

pending-clause.answer: GR7 states its own comparison (binary encoding, no collating sequence, unequal lengths not equal), so it does not rest on §2002:8.8.4.1.1's alphanumeric and national comparison (collating sequence, padding); §2002:8.8.2 concerns boolean operands, not this alphanumeric or national case; §2002:8.8.4.2.4 does not apply to a format-1 >>EVALUATE. No dependency.

behaviour-switch.answer: The switch is DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Control/DialectBehavior.cs:301), read only by CompileTimeArithmetic.For (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeArithmetic.cs:44), which picks the mode for operand entry and + - * / inside a compile-time arithmetic expression (§2002:7.2.5.2 GR1; its 34-digit 2002 mode against §2002:8.8.1.3.1.1's 32 digits is the known PB5575-family defect, reaching only results of arithmetic operations). An alphanumeric or national literal subject is compared by binary encoding, with no arithmetic operation, so the switch cannot reach it.
